caller_ref.description: Optional opaque caller metadata attached to this decision's server-side audit record (when decision logging is enabled): a flat object of string keys to string values, ≤2 KB serialized, no `$`-prefixed or dotted keys. Purely display/narrowing metadata for the caller's own records — it never affects the decision, is never an authorization key, and an invalid value is dropped with a warning rather than rejected.
caller_ref.title: Caller Ref

exclude_fields.description: Field keys the engine must never propose as the next question. Use this for fields a caller has durably given up on (e.g. an applicant refused to answer a field the requisite number of times, so a conversational agent abandoned it): the excluded keys are dropped from `next_question`, `optimal_path`, and the relevance-aware `missing_fields`, so selection routes around them instead of re-proposing the cheapest-but-refused field forever. Excluding a field does not answer it — the outcome may stay `undetermined` if that field was on the only path to a decision.
exclude_fields.title: Exclude Fields

DecideResponse.description:
Outcome of a single `/decide` invocation, plus a reproducibility envelope.

## Reproducibility contract

The envelope is designed to let any caller — aethis-cli, aethis-mcp, a
third-party integration, or an auditor — prove which inputs and which rule
artefact produced a given decision, without the server echoing the inputs
back in the response.

**Replay-critical fields** (retain these with the caller's inputs to
reproduce a decision byte-for-byte on a re-run against the same engine
build and rule artefact):

- `decision_id` — opaque per-invocation audit handle.
- `inputs_hash` — `sha256:<hex>` content hash over the RFC 8785 canonical
  form of the request's `field_values`. Invariant under key reordering.
- `engine_version` — product-prefixed semver of the engine build that
  produced the decision (`aethis-core@<semver>`).
- `ruleset_id` + `ruleset_version` + `content_digest` (ruleset calls)
  **or** `rulebook_id` (rulebook calls) — identifies the rule artefact.
  For a published leaf ruleset all three are always resolved from the
  stored publication (never the caller's slug, never `"unknown"`), on
  both cold and warm cache paths. Richer rulebook pinning with
  `resolved_ruleset_versions` is tracked separately (aethis-core#39);
  until it lands, rulebook replays assume the rulebook's `pin_mode`
  composition has not drifted.

**Blocking-error contract** (issue #330, step 7; see
`aethis_core/public/contracts/decision_truth_table.py`): every
`field_errors` entry is blocking, and a non-empty `field_errors` forces
`decision == "undetermined"` — this response never reports `eligible` or
`not_eligible` beside blocking input errors. Consumers must read
`field_errors` (the structured error channel) rather than inferring
success from present happy-path fields.

**Informational fields** (not part of the replay contract; safe to ignore
when replaying):

- `decision_time` — server UTC timestamp. Required context for any rule
  that references wall-clock time; otherwise informational.
- `timing`, `next_question`, `optimal_path`, `trace`, `explanation`,
  `field_errors`, `section_results`, `missing_fields`.

Server-side audit persistence (storing the envelope plus inputs keyed by
`decision_id` for later lookup) is tracked separately; until it lands,
reliable replay requires the caller to retain the original inputs.

content_digest.description: `sha256:<hex>` digest of the published rule content that produced this decision (replay-critical, ruleset requests only). A republish always changes this value, even when the version label or ruleset_id is reused.
content_digest.title: Content Digest

decision_id.description: Unique identifier for this decision invocation, format `dec_<16 urlsafe chars>`. Fresh per call — two identical requests receive different `decision_id` values, even when the response is served from the decision cache. Use this value when referencing a specific decision in logs, bug reports, or support conversations.
decision_id.title: Decision Id

decision_time.description: Server UTC timestamp at which this decision was made, ISO-8601 with `Z` suffix. Captured once per invocation — identical for cache-hit and cache-miss paths within the same request. Informational for time-independent rules; required context for any rule that references wall-clock time.
decision_time.title: Decision Time

engine_version.description: Product-prefixed semver of the engine build that produced this decision, format `aethis-core@<semver>`. Replay-critical: the decision's outcome is only reproducible under the same engine version unless the engine guarantees backwards-compatible semantics across the versions involved.
engine_version.title: Engine Version

explanation.description: Layered decision explanation, populated when `include_explanation=true` and the request used `ruleset_id`. Shape: `{decision, decision_path?, groups: [{group, status, criteria: [{criterion_id, title, status, supporting_facts?, source_refs?}]}], unused_facts: [field_name, ...]}`. `supporting_facts` lists the answers that proved each satisfied criterion (Or branches report only the satisfied disjunct). `unused_facts` lists provided answers that no satisfied criterion referenced — useful for catching field-name typos.
explanation.title: Explanation

field_errors.description: Blocking input errors, keyed by field id (unknown field key, value that fails the field's type, or an evaluation-time conversion failure). Non-empty field_errors ALWAYS accompanies decision == 'undetermined': the engine never returns a positive/negative terminal verdict computed from a partial input set the caller did not knowingly send.
field_errors.title: Field Errors

graph_overlay.description: Dependency graph (field -> criterion -> group -> outcome) with each criterion node's `overlay` slot stamped from this decision, populated only when `include_graph_overlay=true`. Same shape as the `/rulesets/{id}/graph` (and rulebook `/graph`) response `graph` object: `{nodes, edges, sections, stats}`. Each criterion node carries `overlay: {status: satisfied|not_satisfied|pending, supporting_facts?: [...]}`. Lets a caller render a 'you are here' map of which criteria fired for these inputs. Off by default; absent fields keep the response byte-identical to a call without the flag.
graph_overlay.title: Graph Overlay

inputs_hash.description: Algorithm-prefixed content hash of the request's `field_values`, format `sha256:<64-hex>`. Computed over the RFC 8785 canonical form (sorted keys, NFC-normalised strings, canonical number formatting), so the hash is invariant under key reordering. Lets callers verify that a decision was produced from exactly the inputs they sent, without the server echoing potentially-PII values.
inputs_hash.title: Inputs Hash

ruleset_version.description: Published version label of the decided ruleset (e.g. `v3`). Always resolved from the stored publication for a leaf ruleset — never `unknown` for a published leaf. Rulebook responses report `unknown` until resolved composition identity lands (aethis-core#39).
ruleset_version.title: Ruleset Version

slug.description: Stable, human-readable handle for the ruleset (e.g. `aethis/uk-fsm/child-eligibility`). Set for rulesets published under a slug; null otherwise. Prefer this over `ruleset_id` for documentation, dashboards, and any reference that should survive regeneration — re-publishing under an existing slug rotates the underlying `ruleset_id` while keeping the slug stable.
slug.title: Slug

DecideResponse.title: DecideResponse

ExplainCriterion.description:
One criterion in the ruleset explanation. `source_references` carries
the publish-validated public citation contract — the identical
`SourceReference` DTO POST /decide serves inside
`explanation.groups[].criteria[]` when `include_explanation=true`.

source_references.description: Publish-resolved, validated source references for this criterion. Present only on rulesets published under the fail-closed public citation contract.
source_references.title: Source References

source_refs.description: Opaque authoring citation keys (legacy surface; kept for back-compat).
source_refs.title: Source Refs

ExplainCriterion.title: ExplainCriterion

content_digest.description: sha256:<hex> digest of the published rule content.
content_digest.title: Content Digest

ruleset_id.description: Resolved immutable ruleset ID (never the caller's slug).
ruleset_id.title: Ruleset Id

ruleset_version.description: Published version label of this ruleset.
ruleset_version.title: Ruleset Version

FieldNoteOut.description:
Public-API shape for a single structured note attached to a field.

Mirrors the internal `FieldNote` (`storage.models.schemas.FieldNote` /
`elig.eligibility_navigator.FieldNote`). The `metadata` dict is left
loosely-typed because callers attach domain-specific tags
(`type`, `section`, `warning`, ...).

metadata.description: Structured tags. Conventionally includes `type` (`why` | `legal_background`), `section`, and optionally `warning: true` for rarely-granted routes.
metadata.title: Metadata

note_text.description: Note body. Plain text; may span multiple paragraphs.
note_text.title: Note Text

source.description: Citation for the note — typically a Home Office guidance page title, a statute reference, or a URL drawn from the ruleset's provenance pack.
source.title: Source

FieldNoteOut.title: FieldNoteOut

enum_values.description: Closed set of allowed values when `sort` is `Enum`; `None` for every other sort (and when the type could not be resolved). Mirrors `/schema`'s `FieldInfo.enum_values`.
enum_values.title: Enum Values

notes.description: Structured guidance attached to the field being asked. Surfaces the same notes the navigator appends to its internal extraction prompts so callers can render rationale and legal background to end users alongside the question.
notes.title: Notes

sort.description: Answer type of the field being asked (`Int` / `Bool` / `String` / `Enum` / `Date` / `Duration`), when known. Lets callers render a typed input affordance (yes/no chips, a date picker, an option list) without a second `/schema` round-trip. `None` when the type could not be resolved for this field. Serialised as the sort's string value, matching `/schema`'s `FieldInfo.sort`.

x_ui_widget.description: Authoring override for the UI-affordance layer, carried through from the field's `FieldDefinition.x_ui_widget`. Currently only `free_text` is recognised: it tells the caller to suppress the schema-derived structured-answer affordance (chips / select / date-picker) for this field and render a plain text composer, even though `sort` is set. `None` when no override is authored. Mirrors `/schema`'s `FieldInfo.x_ui_widget`.
x_ui_widget.title: X Ui Widget

Sort.description:
Primitive sorts supported by the rule engine.

Maps to the constraint solver's primitive sorts. Dates and durations are represented as Int (days).
Sort.title: Sort

SourceQuote.description:
The verbatim text a reference cites, with optional locating context.

``exact`` MUST occur verbatim in the fetched source whose
``content_digest`` is recorded on the parent reference — publish
validation enforces this and fails closed on a non-occurring quote.
Modelled on the W3C Web Annotation TextQuoteSelector.

exact.description: Verbatim quoted text from the cited source. Never a summary or paraphrase — publish validation asserts this text occurs in the fetched source verbatim after whitespace normalisation (HTML is tag-stripped; PDF is checked against extracted page text). No stemming, case folding or fuzzy matching.
exact.title: Exact

prefix.description: Optional short verbatim context immediately before the quote.
prefix.title: Prefix

suffix.description: Optional short verbatim context immediately after the quote.
suffix.title: Suffix

SourceQuote.title: SourceQuote

SourceReference.description: One publish-validated citation binding a criterion to its authority.

authority.description: Publisher / issuing authority of the cited document.
authority.title: Authority

content_digest.description: sha256:<hex> digest of the exact bytes fetched from `url` at publish-time verification.
content_digest.title: Content Digest

deep_link.description: Self-locating link derived from url + quote: a percent-encoded `#:~:text=` text fragment for HTML/text sources, `#page=N` for PDF sources (N from the locator when it names a page).
deep_link.title: Deep Link

licence.description: Licence under which the cited text is reproduced (e.g. 'OGL-UK-3.0'). Publishing an unlicensed reference fails closed.
licence.title: Licence

locator.description: Section/paragraph/page locator within the document, when available.
locator.title: Locator

media_type.description: Media type of the fetched source; selects the deep-link form.
media_type.title: Media Type

quote.description: The verbatim cited text (never a summary), verified against the digested source.

schema_version.description: Wire-schema version of this reference. Additive evolution only: v2 will add an uploaded-source referent (aethis-core#331) without breaking v1 consumers.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

source_date.description: Publication/revision date of the cited document (ISO 8601), when available.
source_date.title: Source Date

source_id.description: Stable opaque identifier of this reference within its published ruleset version (the authoring citation key, e.g. 'BNA1981#Schedule1/P1.1').
source_id.title: Source Id

source_version.description: Version label of the cited document, when the authority publishes one.
source_version.title: Source Version

title.description: Human-meaningful title of the cited document.
title.title: Title

url.description: HTTPS URL of the cited document, validated at publish time (HTTPS only; no credentials, IP literals or private/reserved destinations; bounded redirects/size/time).
url.title: Url

verified_at.description: UTC time the target was fetched, digested and the quote verified.
verified_at.title: Verified At

SourceReference.title: SourceReference
